subject: Clarify scope: derived output, training constraints, and feedback license
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novum.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@novum.ai>, Novum Contracts <contracts@novum.ai>
Date: 2027-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novum redlines: IP, outputs, and training carveouts

Hi Soojin,

Attached is Novum's redline of the MSA and the proposed order form. The commercial team surfaced three items that are blockers for legal:

- Output ownership: Novum requires an express confirmation that customer users retain ownership of Outputs generated by their prompts and data.
- Training/data use: Novum wants firm language that Novum Customer Data and customer-specific prompts will not be used to train Redwood models (or derivatives) without an explicit written opt-in.
- Feedback license: Novum is okay with operational telemetry, but wants any use of customer-provided content for model improvement limited to aggregated, de-identified data and subject to an opt-in.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept these as redlines or if you need counter language. Also include any commercial tradeoffs (credits/discounts) that would be required in exchange for more liberal training rights.

Attachment: Novum_MSA_redline_20270803.docx (redline + inline comments)

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Counsel, Novum AI
elena.morales@novum.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Novum redlines: IP, outputs, and training carveouts

Aditya / Kimberly — forwarding Novum's redline (attached). Key asks summarized above. My read: Novum is asking for fairly strict carveouts that would limit our ability to use customer data for ongoing model improvements.

Proposed approach:
- Sales (Aditya): raise a commercial counter-offer — Novum can retain Output ownership but we ask for a bounded training window (e.g., 12 months) during which we can use anonymized usage signals for model tuning, or provide a pricing credit if they opt out of training entirely.
- Legal (Kimberly): propose precise contract language that preserves customer Output rights while allowing Redwood to retain a narrowly-scoped, de-identified feedback license for service improvement. Avoid broad "use for training" language unless there's an explicit opt-in.

Action items:
1) Aditya — please draft two commercial options (opt-out with credit; opt-in for training with a small uplift) and confirm with Novum if a short pilot is acceptable.
2) Kimberly — can you propose replacement clauses for "Training Data" and "Feedback License" that we can send as a marked counter? If you need escalation parameters, flag them here.

I'll hold a 30-min sync after we have draft language.

Attachment: Novum_MSA_redline_20270803.docx

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Legal Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Novum redlines: IP, outputs, and training carveouts

Quick commercial note from my side — I spoke with Novum's product lead this morning. They need a clean guarantee on Outputs for their engineering and investor teams. They are sensitive about "training" because they see model retraining as product differentiation.

What I can offer them (two options):
A) Strict opt-out: Novum retains exclusive control of Outputs and all Customer Data is excluded from model training. In exchange, Redwood would apply a 15% platform-credit (annual) or a 10% uplift on list pricing if they want to opt back in later.
B) Time-limited training window: Novum retains Output ownership; Redwood may use de-identified Customer Data for internal model improvements for a 12-month window after data is first processed. After 12 months, continued training would require written consent and an additional commercial agreement.

I'll push Novum on B first and see if they'll accept a 12-month window. I've drafted a clean Order Form that outlines option B and pricing impacts — attached (RDW-Proposed-OrderForm-20270803.pdf).

If Legal can draft the narrower language today, I can send both the redline + commercial options to Novum later this afternoon.

Attachment: RDW-Proposed-OrderForm-20270803.pdf

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

On Tue, Aug 3, 2027 at 09:12 AM Elena Morales <elena.morales@novum.ai> wrote:
> Attached is Novum's redline of the MSA and the proposed order form.

I reviewed Novum's comments and Aditya's commercial options. Below is proposed contract language that preserves customer Output rights while protecting Redwood's ability to operate and improve the service in a limited way. Please review and let me know if you want me to mark this into the MSA redline.

Proposed replacements / clarifications:

1) Outputs and Ownership.
"Customer Outputs" means text, files or other content produced by the Service in response to Customer Data or prompts submitted by Customer users. Customer retains all rights, title and interest in and to Customer Outputs. Redwood shall not assert ownership over Customer Outputs.

2) Training Data; Prohibition Unless Opt-In.
"Customer Data" (including prompts and files) shall not be used to train, fine-tune, or update Redwood's models or underlying weights without Customer's prior express written consent.

3) Feedback and Service Improvement License.
"Feedback" (including usage telemetry, performance metrics, and error logs) may be collected by Redwood and used solely to improve the Service provided that such Feedback is aggregated and de-identified such that it cannot reasonably be re-associated with Customer or any natural person. Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual license to use Feedback solely for diagnostic, security, analytics, and service improvement purposes.

Notes / redlines:
- If Sales wants the 12-month window (Option B) for limited model tuning, we should add a specific carveout that enumerates the types of processing permitted, require technical controls (e.g., separate datasets, no linking to customer IDs), and a contractual auditing right.
- We should avoid language that permits "derivative" training rights; derivatives are a slippery term and often interpreted broadly. If Novum insists on derivative usage, require explicit examples and a narrow definition.
- For any opt-in to training, require a separate Amendment and confirm data retention and deletion timelines.

If you want, I will prepare a marked MSA with the above language and include a short memo explaining the tradeoffs for the commercial team.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novum.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-08-03T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Novum redlines: IP, outputs, and training carveouts

Soojin, Aditya, Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft language. Novum legal and product like the Feedback carve (aggregated + de-identified), and the explicit prohibition on using Customer Data for training without opt-in. A couple of outstanding items before we mark:

1) The 12-month time-limited training window — is that negotiable? Novum's CTO would prefer a permanent opt-out unless we can point to a strong commercial rationale for allowing time-limited use.
2) Derivative outputs: can you put a sample definition in the marked MSA that clarifies whether "derivative outputs" include model-generated summaries, embeddings, or synthesized code? We need explicit examples to evaluate risk.
3) Outputs monetization: confirm that Novum may use Outputs produced by their users in their products without royalty or attribution to Redwood.

If you can send a marked redline incorporating Kimberly's text plus a short sample "derivative" definition (bullet list), we can route internally and get sign-off. If the 12-month window is required by Redwood, flag the commercial uplift you're asking for (Aditya's options would be fine to circulate).

Thanks — I'll plan to reconvene with Novum product/legal after your mark.

Elena Morales
Counsel, Novum AI
elena.morales@novum.ai
